steps.text: Spray 4 cookie sheets with cooking spray; sprinkle with anise seeds and set aside until needed.

Mix flour and baking powder together in a large bowl until well blended. Place sugar, eggs, and vanilla in a separate large bowl; beat with an electric mixer until light and frothy, 5 to 8 minutes. Gradually stir flour mixture into egg mixture to form a thick dough.

Working with handfuls of dough at a time, roll out onto a lightly floured surface until 1/4 inch thick. Lightly sift confectioners' sugar over dough. Place springerle molds onto dough; press down hard and evenly until the mold's design registers in dough. Remove the mold. Use a small knife to cut around each cookie, and place them 2 inches apart on the prepared cookie sheets. Repeat, until all dough has been used. Cover cookies with a lightweight cotton cloth, and allow to dry for 8 hours, or overnight. The designs will remain embossed in the cookies.
When ready to bake, preheat the oven to 250 degrees F (120 degrees C).
Bake cookies in preheated oven until tops are pale brown and cookies are set, 25 to 30 minutes. Transfer to a wire rack to cool completely. Store in an airtight container.

raw_recipe.headline: Traditional Springerle
raw_recipe.description: Springerle cookies are a centuries-old, anise-flavored German Christmas cookie made using decorative, carved wooden molds or rolling pins that let the designs remain embossed in the cookies when baked.
raw_recipe.name: Traditional Springerle

review.reviewBody: UPDATE! My mother called a few weeks ago and mentioned that she had tried making a variation for Valentine's Day with the zest of an orange and 1/8 tsp orange oil. AMAZING! and beautiful pressed with a springerle mold and then cut with a heart shaped cookie cutter!

Update!2019 - I used wilton luster dust in 2018 and it was horrible! Went back to oasis pearl and pharaohs gold I got on Amazon awesome! I tried 3 different springerle recipes including martha's- this is the best tasting recipe by far!! And will be my permanent recipe from now on. Taste and texture are the most authentic. Originally i added way more flour however from now on I will add more flour as needed when rolling. - reg flour is best! No need for cake flour or over beating eggs like other recipes suggest I painted mine with luster dust and pinch of anise extract. MIX the extract and dust in a little bowl with small paint brush. Update! 4 th year making! IF you don't want powdered sugar or flour on cookies so you can paint them spray molds with Pam instead of dusting w/sugar. Also I keep additional flour to a minimum for softer dough that way you can just press molds with hands instead of using a mallet. Honestly I didn't even use rolling pin this year I just flattened dough w/ my hands then pressed pam spray molds on. Design stayed put - nice clean cookie to paint! My cookies are the first 7 photos for reference with and without powdered sugar dust. I highly recommended keeping dough as moist as you can and still be able to roll. There's no need to add excess flour your imprint will remain without it! I do notice the imprint is better when I use flour instead of Pam so if your not painting just flour your "molds" really good not the dough!

I loved this recipe! I love the chewy texture, so I was happy they stayed chewy even after 3 to 4 days. I added lemon zest to the dough and that made for a great flavor. I tried to use the springerle mold I had, but the impression was deep and the dough was too sticky so I switched over to an embossed rolling pin and they turned out beautifully!! I’ll definitely be making these again!!

I have been making springerles for over fifty years. I've used this recipe several times. My only comment might be to give folks a realistic time frame for how long it does take to actually form the cookies. Depending on which forms are used, it could take several times the preparation time stated in the recipe.

I remember eating this when I was a kid from our local bakery. So I used your recipe and it turned out excellent. I rolled out the dough with a regular rolling pin then I used a special rolling pin for the imprint. Absolutely fabulous! Thank You Karen M
Mine were too moist to start also. I just added more flour to get them to roll out. And I added anise oil to get a stronger flavor.

I've been making Schpringerle for over 20 years for Christmas, a German tradition. This is a very good recipe. Definitely need to add lemon zest. To those far away (Australia ), may I suggest logging on to the King Arthur Flour website to locate moulds or rolling pin. Happy Baking!

I, too, have many molds from House on the Hill, and have used their recipe, which is much more fussy than this. The molds are stunning; they'd better be for the cost, and people are always blown away by them-as if I carved each cookie myself! I have found that crimped cookie cutter shapes--square, rectangle, circle, do a nice job of finishing the cookies. I have also used stamps intended for ink to make nice impressions. I love "painting" the cookies with various food coloring recipes, although I have not found one that is quite what I'm looking for--does anyone out there have suggestions for this?
Easy, great flavor & texture. Family loves them. I guess we have started a new Christmas cookie tradition!

My dough was waaaaay too moist. I added a lot of flour to make it workable. I also added lemon zest and did not add the anise seeds. The dough stuck to my mild quite a bit, so I abandoned ship and just used my regular old cookie cutters. I'll try a more traditional recipe next time.

I actually used the press with Santa and his reindeer flying over the village pictured at the top of this recipe. The dough was challenging to work with because of its tendency to stick to the press. In most cases you cannot make out the scene, which is the point of using a Springerle press.

This was my first attempt at springerle. The first rollout turned out predictably not very uniform or pretty. But once i got the hang of it, the rest are adorable! I ate one of the practice ones warm out of the oven. I was skeptical whether the seeds would provide enough anise flavor. I know it will get stronger with aging. But it is already very evident. Lovely, eggy, vanilla-y... and anise. Just perfect.

My mother used to make Springerle. I loved them but I never learned how to make them. After she died, we couldn't find her recipe. I've been searching for something close to what she made, and this is it! They came out perfect the first try. So delighted with these - I was actually getting teary after I tasted the first one!

This is my first time trying these cookies and I agree with what most have said. They turn out great! At first, I didn't have enough powdered sugar on top and the mold stuck, but I got it the second round.

Love this recipe....I am so happy with the detail on my impressions - clear and crisp. They seemed to become crisper after baking. I use a pastry brush to brush off excess powdered sugar after they have baked and cooled. Looking forward to using this recipe and playing around with different flavors.

The recipe is sound and I think my issue was user error, or at least inexperience. Also, I didn't use anise seeds since DH doesn't like anise. Instead I used 1/4 t of orange oil. They are tasty for sure, but they poofed up a LOT. I'm thinking maybe I didn't let them dry long enough before baking. Not a total disaster, but not photo-worthy either.
